dream_job.statement: I want to keep building LLM systems that actually work in production, not just demos. The sweet spot for me is a role where I'm the technical lead for a small team of engineers, designing and shipping RAG pipelines, agentic workflows, and fine-tuned models that solve real business problems. Day to day, that means writing Python, wrestling with LangChain or raw APIs, tuning prompts, and debugging why a retrieval call is slow or returning garbage. I want to be deep in the code, but also setting the technical direction and mentoring others. The ideal company is one that already has data infrastructure and is serious about putting LLMs into customer-facing products—maybe in manufacturing, logistics, or energy, where I've built domain expertise. I want to work with a platform team that values MLOps and LLMOps, where we use MLflow, Kubernetes, and proper CI/CD. I'm done with being the guy who just wires up APIs without thinking about evaluation, cost, or latency. I want to stop doing endless stakeholder demos and slide decks. I want to stop maintaining legacy data pipelines that have nothing to do with AI. And I absolutely won't take a role that's just 'prompt engineer' with no engineering ownership. Deal-breakers: no real engineering ownership; no existing data infrastructure; no budget for GPU or cloud compute.

planted_conflicts.why: The CV states the legal entity, the export states the brand. The merge still pairs the role because company_variants strips the legal form, so the disagreement is reported rather than read as two separate jobs.

The CV ends the role three months before the export does - the ordinary drift of a CV rewritten from memory. Both readings are month-precise, so _same_date reports a real disagreement rather than a rounding gap.
